<parameter name="content"># Claude Code context layout for `atlas`

Principle: always-loaded context (root CLAUDE.md) holds only what every task needs. Service quirks load only when working in that service. Long procedures load on demand (skills). Things that must never happen are enforced by hooks and permissions, not by prose. External data access goes through MCP.

## Files and mechanisms

| Location | Mechanism | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `/CLAUDE.md` | Root memory file, always loaded | Org-wide conventions (conventional commits, `make check` before PR, trunk-based) plus a map of the three services; short so it costs little on every task. |
| `/api/CLAUDE.md` | Subdirectory memory, loaded when Claude works under `api/` | Holds the Go/gRPC notes and the `api/gen/` "generated, run `make proto`" rule, so web and pipeline sessions never pay for it. |
| `/web/CLAUDE.md` | Subdirectory memory | Holds the `npm run test:unit` vs `npm test` (Playwright, opens real browsers) distinction where it is relevant. |
| `/pipeline/CLAUDE.md` | Subdirectory memory | Holds the requirement to set `AIRFLOW_HOME=pipeline/.airflow` before importing or testing DAGs. |
| `/.claude/settings.json` hook (PreToolUse on Edit/Write for `api/gen/**`) | Hook | The silent-overwrite hazard is a hard rule; a hook denies the edit with a message pointing to `make proto`, which is more reliable than a prose instruction. |
| `/.claude/settings.json` permissions | Permission rules | Allow `make check`, `make proto`, `npm run test:unit`; keep bare `npm test` on "ask" so browsers are not launched by accident. |
| `incident-response` skill (`SKILL.md`, 20 steps) | Skill, distributed via a company-wide plugin or the org's managed settings, not stored in atlas | The runbook is identical for every team, so one shared source of truth avoids drift. A skill loads only when invoked, so 20 steps never sit in everyday context. |
| `.mcp.json` warehouse server (read-only credentials) | MCP server, scoped to the analyst workflow | Live SQL needs a real tool and credentials, which CLAUDE.md can't provide. A read-only role and a permission prompt on queries bound the risk. Credentials come from env vars, never committed. |
| `analytics-metrics` skill (optional) | Skill | Documents warehouse tables, metric definitions and query etiquette; loads only when someone asks about product metrics. |
| `CLAUDE.local.md` (gitignored) | Personal memory | Individual preferences and local paths stay out of the shared repo. |

## What deliberately stays out of the root CLAUDE.md
- The 20-step runbook (skill; shared across the company).
- Warehouse access and SQL guidance (MCP + skill; only analysts need it).
- Per-service quirks (subdirectory files).
- Anything derivable from the code, such as directory trees or dependency lists.

## Notes
- If the org-wide conventions must be identical across every repo, they could move to a managed-policy CLAUDE.md; the root file would then only reference them.
- If `AIRFLOW_HOME` keeps being forgotten, set it in a `make` target or wrapper script so the correct environment is the default, and keep the CLAUDE.md line as documentation.

<parameter name="content"># atlas

Monorepo with three services:
- `api/`: Go, gRPC
- `web/`: React/TypeScript
- `pipeline/`: Python, Airflow

Each service has its own `CLAUDE.md` with service-specific rules. Read it before working in that directory.

## Conventions (all services)
- Use conventional commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, etc.).
- `make check` must pass before opening any PR.
- Trunk-based development: short-lived branches only, no long-lived branches.

## Gotchas to know up front
- `api/gen/` is generated by `make proto`. Never hand-edit it; regenerate instead.
- `web/`: `npm test` launches real browsers via Playwright. Use `npm run test:unit` for unit tests.
- `pipeline/`: set `AIRFLOW_HOME=pipeline/.airflow` before anything that imports DAGs.

## Other workflows
- Incident response: use the `incident-response` skill; do not improvise the runbook.
- Product metrics questions: use the warehouse MCP tool (read-only) rather than guessing figures.
